transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hi, I'm Dora. I'm a clinical conversational agent, and I'm here to help you with any questions you might have about your cataract surgery recovery. Do you have any questions for me today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi, yes I do have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You can go back to light exercise, like gardening, one week after surgery. Just be sure to avoid strenuous activities for a month. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Great, thank you. When can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: If you were using eye drops for dry eyes before your operation, it's safe to continue using them, unless you've been told otherwise. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Okay, that's helpful. I'm feeling very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended: It's normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust. If it's mild and things just seem brighter, wearing sunglasses when you go outside is recommended. However, if you have significant pain when it's bright, or severe light sensitivity, especially if your eye is also red and painful, we may need to assess this further. Do you have any other questions?
